name: Battersea Park
highlights: A quiet inner-city riverside park with a flat carriage-drive loop, an athletics track and views across the Thames.

name: Kensington Gardens & Hyde Park
highlights: Two of London's grandest royal parks joined into one 7km perimeter loop past the Serpentine, palaces and the Albert Memorial.

name: St James's Park & Green Park
highlights: A photogenic pair of royal parks around Buckingham Palace, linked by The Mall, with an easy flat loop and lake views.

name: Regent's Park & Primrose Hill
highlights: Everything a runner could want: flat playing fields, a running track, gardens, a canal and the famous city view from Primrose Hill.

name: Burgess Park
highlights: A regenerated south London park with a fishing lake, man-made hills for sprints and the traffic-free old Surrey Canal alignment toward Peckham.

name: Southwark Park & Docks
highlights: A Victorian park that links via the old Rotherhithe docks to the Thames Path.

name: Victoria Park
highlights: The model east London park: tree-lined avenues, a boating lake and a flat perimeter loop, with canal towpaths on its doorstep.

name: The Grand Tour
highlights: An hour-long sightseeing loop past nearly every major London landmark: Big Ben, the London Eye, Tower Bridge, St Paul's and the Thames bridges.

name: Diana Memorial Run
highlights: A way-marked figure-of-eight through four royal parks, tracing brass plaques past Buckingham Palace, the Serpentine and the Diana Memorial Fountain.

name: Regent's Canal
highlights: A largely traffic-free nine-mile towpath run through London's heart, from the East End past Camden Lock and Regent's Park to the tranquillity of Little Venice.
